Lakshmi. The goddess of wealth, fortune, abundance, and prosperity in Hindu tradition.

Lakshmi is the eternal consort of Vishnu and embodies his shakti, his divine power. She appears at his side in all his incarnations and cosmic forms. As the goddess of wealth and prosperity, she represents both material and spiritual riches. She embodies grace, beauty, and the blessings that flow from living according to dharma.

She is depicted adorned in gold and jewels, often seated or standing on a lotus flower. The lotus symbolizes purity rising from worldly existence. She holds lotus flowers and pours coins from her hands, representing the continuous flow of blessings and generosity.

Lakshmi is worshipped especially during Diwali, the festival of lights, when homes are cleaned and decorated to invite her blessings. She is associated with lakshya, which means goal, and the achievement of auspicious aims through devotion and righteous living.

She is believed to withdraw from those who act unethically or with greed, rewarding virtue and punishing vice. In this way, she embodies the moral dimension of abundance—wealth and good fortune are meant for those who live righteously.

She is often depicted with four arms, each holding a lotus, a pot of gold, and a gesture of blessing and protection. Through these symbols, Lakshmi represents the complete flow of prosperity and divine care in the world.
